title: MQM-P urges national dialogue to finalise framework for creation of new provinces
description: MQM-P says population growth demands new administrative units.Party may approach Supreme Court over stalled provinces issue.PM's adviser rejects consideration of any plan for new provinces.Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan Chairman...
content: Published August 16, 2026 Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) Chairman Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui on Sunday called for a national dialogue on the creation of new provinces, saying Pakistan's existing administrative structure no longer corresponds to the country's demographic realities and governance requirements. The call comes amid a renewed debate on administrative reforms after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi proposed last month the creation of new administrative units, arguing that Pakistan's "collapsed" governance structure requires restructuring to meet growing administrative challenges. Siddiqui, addressing a press conference alongside senior MQM-P leaders Dr Farooq Sattar and Mustafa Kamal in Karachi, urged political parties to rise above partisan differences and build a consensus on administrative reforms. He argued that the issue should be addressed through an inclusive national discussion rather than political confrontation. He said support for the proposal was growing across the political spectrum, adding that MQM-P was prepared to engage with all stakeholders to develop a framework for the establishment of new provinces where they were needed. Siddiqui maintained that Pakistan's provinces were originally formed on linguistic considerations and had since evolved into large administrative units. Despite substantial population growth over the decades, he said, successive governments had created numerous districts while avoiding a broader debate on provincial reorganisation. "The effects of not creating new provinces should also be discussed," he said, arguing that administrative boundaries should reflect population size and governance needs. He added that Sindh was among the regions where the demand for additional administrative units was most pronounced. The MQM-P chairman rejected the notion that advocating new provinces was controversial, noting that the Constitution itself contains provisions relating to the creation of provinces. "If it is considered an act of disloyalty, then why does the Constitution provide for it?" he asked. Referring to the 18th Constitutional Amendment, Siddiqui said his party supported the reforms to ensure that the benefits of democracy reached all parts of the country. He argued, however, that the objectives of decentralisation could not be fully realised without strengthening administrative structures at the provincial level. He said MQM-P had already introduced a constitutional bill on the issue, which remains before a parliamentary standing committee, and recalled that the party had previously sought judicial intervention when progress stalled. Siddiqui said MQM-P would continue supporting calls for new provinces from different parts of the country and remained open to dialogue with all political parties. He also indicated that the party could again approach the Supreme Court if constitutional and legal obligations regarding the matter remained unfulfilled. Kamal said that the creation of additional administrative units was not aimed against any ethnic group, including Sindhis, but was intended to improve governance and public representation. He said a more decentralised administrative structure would give citizens greater influence over local governance and strengthen accountability. Addressing the presser, Sattar said the establishment of additional administrative units has become essential for the country's stability and cohesion. He was of the view that bringing governance closer to citizens would improve public participation, enhance service delivery and ensure that local leadership emerged from the areas it represented. The proposal has, however, elicited mixed reactions across the political spectrum. The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), which governs Sindh and is a key coalition partner of the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N), has firmly opposed the creation of new provinces. Senior government figures, including Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Prime Minister's Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, have also refrained from endorsing the idea. As the debate gathered momentum, Naqvi moved to clarify his earlier remarks, rejecting suggestions that he had criticised the government. He said he was part of the administration and would not issue a "charge sheet" against his own government. Speaking to Geo News , the interior minister had said the current system would continue and complete its constitutional term, stressing that his comments about a "collapsed" governance structure referred to the gradual erosion of administrative and institutional capacity over the past eight decades rather than the performance of the present government. A day ago, Sanaullah said that the government had not formulated any plan regarding the creation of new provinces. Speaking on Geo News programme Naya Pakistan, he noted that various proposals were being floated publicly, with some advocating 12 provinces, others 20, and some even more. He said MQM-P leader and Federal Minister Kamal's proposal was primarily focused on Karachi, adding that the PML-N's top leadership had not discussed the issue in recent days. He also questioned the level of public support for the proposal, arguing that there was no widespread demand for new provinces across the country. Apart from calls for a Hazara province, he said, there was little evidence of a broader grassroots movement in favour of provincial reorganisation. The proposal has, however, found support in some political quarters. Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party (IPP) President Abdul Aleem Khan backed the creation of new provinces, describing it as a national issue that should not be sacrificed for political expediency. He also voiced support for the establishment of South Punjab and Bahawalpur provinces, saying demands for additional administrative units were emerging from different parts of the country. Major opposition party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan also endorsed the idea, saying the country required additional administrative units. He stressed, however, that any move to create new provinces should be based on broad political consensus and carried out through the constitutional process, including approval by the requisite two-thirds majority in the relevant assemblies. title: KP govt rejects Rs6.4bn cut in federal financial transfers
description: Finance Ministry proposed direct deduction: Sohail Afridi.Says KP govt did not sign an MoU on share deduction.Vows KP govt won't compromise on constitutional right.PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government has refused to accept...
content: Published August 15, 2026 PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government has refused to accept an Rs6.4 billion deduction from its federal financial transfers proposed by the Centre. In a statement, Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said the federal government had sought an additional amount from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa before the budget, adding that releasing the provision had been made conditional on a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan and his approval. He said his provincial government did not sign a memorandum of understanding regarding the additional amount as he was not granted permission to meet the PTI founder. He said that if the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) achieved its Rs15,260 billion target, the province's share would amount to Rs175 billion. Ahead of the passage of Budget 2026-27, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said the provinces had provided a grant to the federal government for defence requirements and to create a buffer against the second and third-order impacts of the ongoing Gulf region conflict. "This arrangement with the provinces has been struck for three years, and it has nothing to do with the National Finance Commission," he said at his post-budget press conference on June 13. CM Afridi said another condition was that the merged districts be given their rightful share in the 11th NFC. He said the federal government accepted this condition and incorporated it into the proceedings of the National Economic Council. It was also decided that if the merged districts did not receive their share within six months, a summary would be prepared and an ordinance issued under the 7th NFC. He added that the additional federal grant was not included in KP's provincial budget for 2026-27. The chief minister said the Ministry of Finance proposed on August 5 that Rs6.4 billion owed to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa be deducted directly. "The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government neither approved nor agreed to the proposed Rs6.4 billion deduction," he said. The provincial Finance Department subsequently made its opposition clear in a letter dated August 13. Afridi said the issue was not merely a political disagreement but concerned the province's constitutional and financial rights. He said Finance Adviser Muzammil Aslam immediately met relevant officials of the Accountant General Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, following which written instructions were issued against making any deduction without the province's consent. The Accountant General Pakistan Revenues had also been instructed not to record or implement any transaction without the provincial government's explicit consent. He said Article 164 of the Constitution did not give the federal government the authority to unilaterally deduct amounts owed to the province, and that any deduction required a clear constitutional or legal basis as well as provincial consent. The chief minister said the KP government had already filed a petition before the Federal Constitutional Court to secure its constitutional right under the NFC and would pursue every legal and constitutional avenue to protect its financial share. "The provincial government will not compromise on its NFC rights," he said. Copyright © 2026. Geo Television Network. All Rights Reserved. | Contact Us | Authors | Privacy Policy

title: President Zardari approves civil awards for 355 personalities from diverse fields
description: Journalists, artists and athletes feature among award recipients.Security personnel and martyrs to receive gallantry awards.Foreign dignitaries, overseas Pakistanis will also receive honours.President Asif Ali Zardari has approved...
content: Published August 15, 2026 President Asif Ali Zardari has approved civil awards for 355 individuals in recognition of their contributions to a wide range of fields, including science, education, medicine, arts, sports and public service. The list includes federal ministers, government officials, academics, doctors, journalists, artists, writers, athletes, philanthropists, security personnel, police officers, martyrs and foreign dignitaries, The News reported. Ministers recommended for Nishan-i-Imtiaz: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Finance and Revenue Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Federal Minister for Establishment and Economic Affairs Ahad Khan Cheema and Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, all of whom have been recommended for Nishan-i-Imtiaz, Hafiz Muhammad Tahir Mehmood Ashrafi — Tamgha-i-Imtiaz under the public service category. The list further recommends Intelligence Bureau Director General Fuad Asadullah, Attorney General Mansoor Usman Awan, Finance Division Secretary Imdadullah Bosal, FBR Chairman Rashid Mahmood Lagrial and Establishment Division Secretary Nabeel A. Awan for Hilal-i-Imtiaz. A large number of other serving and former public servants have also been recommended for Sitara-i-Imtiaz and Tamgha-i-Imtiaz, including officials from the finance, revenue, police, administration, commerce, law and other government sectors. In the science category, Dr Shahid Mahmud, CEO/Chairman of Interactive Group of Companies, has been recommended for Hilal-i-Imtiaz. Prof Dr Syed Zafar Ilyas and Prof Dr Mudassir Asrar have been proposed for Sitara-i-Imtiaz, while Dr Sajjad Hussain, Prof Dr Aneela Zameer Jaffery and Dr Urooj Saeed have been recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz. The engineering category includes Dr Muhammad Sadiq, Vice Chancellor of UET Peshawar, and Prof Dr Naeemul Haq Tariq, Principal Engineer/Professor at PIEAS, both recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz. title: Forces eliminate 10 terrorists in Khuzdar operation - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
description: Several others injured as three hideouts targeted in Shor Pard; search underway for those who escaped.
content: Get the latest news and updates from Dawn • Several others injured as three hideouts targeted in Shor Pard • Search underway for those who escaped QUETTA: Security forces killed 10 terrorists and injured many others in an intelligence-based operation in Shor Pard area of Khuzdar district on Saturday. During the operation, security forces cordoned off and engaged multiple terrorist hideouts. Accor­ding to security sources, the terrorists were operating in three separate groups, leading to an intense exchange of fire with the security forces. “As a result of the operation, 10 terrorists were killed, while several others sustained injuries,” security sources said. They said that following the engagement, security forces launched an extensive search and clearance operation across the surrounding area. Efforts were underway to track down the terrorists who managed to escape. Security forces have reaffirmed their determination to continue targeted operations against terrorist elements and to eliminate the threat of terrorism from the region. They pledged that the search operation would continue until all remaining terrorists were located and brought to justice. Tribute paid to forces Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to security forces for the successful operation in the mountainous region of Shor Parod, state-run APP reported. “Security forces killed 10 terrorists in a successful operation. Successful operations against terrorists who are enemies of humanity, are a manifestation of the expertise of our security forces,” he said in a statement. “The entire nation is with the security forces in the war against terrorism. We are determined to completely eradicate terrorism from the country,” he added. The development came a day after Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove survived an armed attack on his convoy while returning to Quetta after attending a flag-hoisting ceremony in Kalat. Armed men hiding in the mountains targeted the convoy in the Kund Umrani area of Khad Kocha as it travelled along the Quetta-Karachi National Highway, injuring nine people, including seven police personnel deployed to protect the minister. On Wednesday, the military’s media wing said eight terrorists were killed when explosive material detonated during the preparation of a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device in the Surab district of Balochistan. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, security forces launched a comprehensive clearance operation following the explosion on Monday morning, tracking down and killing another 10 terrorists affiliated with Fitna Al Hindustan. The initial explosion of explosive material also resulted in civilian casualties and ISPR said that at least three civilians lost their lives in a secondary detonation of other explosives stored at the terrorists’ hideout. “In total, 18 terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan have been eliminated so far,” the ISPR said, adding that two soldiers were injured during an exchange of fire. title: Pakistan embassy unveils Qu­aid’s statue in Washington - World - DAWN.COM
description: The statue, donated by the Quaid-i-Azam Foundation of Houston, will remain permanently at the embassy.
content: Get the latest news and updates from Dawn WASHINGTON: A statue of Qu­aid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah was unveiled at the Pakistan Embassy in Washington on Friday, giving the country’s Independence Day celebrations a distinctly historical dimension and placing the founder of Pakis­tan at the centre of a ceremony that also highlighted the evolving Pakistan-United States relationship. Ambassador of Pakistan to the US Rizwan Saeed Sheikh unvei­led the statue during an Indepen­dence Day ceremony attended by members of the Pakistani-American community, diplomats and media representatives. The statue, donated by the Quaid-i-Azam Foundation of Houston, will remain permanently at the embassy. Its unveiling comes as Pakistan prepares to mark Jinnah’s 150th birth anniversary later this year. Paying tribute to the founder, Ambassador Sheikh said the nati­­on remained grateful to Mr Jin­nah for his constitutional struggle and tireless efforts that turned the idea of Pakistan into a reality. “The inspiring leadership of Quaid-i-Azam united the Muslims of the subcontinent under one flag and blessed us with freedom,” he said, urging Pakistanis, particularly those living abroad, to uphold Jinnah’s principles of “Unity, Faith and Discipline”. The Independence Day ceremony began with the hoisting of the national flag to the strains of the national anthem, followed by the recitation of verses from the Holy Quran and the reading of messages from Pakistan’s president, prime minister and deputy prime minister. In his address, Ambassador Sheikh used the occasion to underline Pakistan’s continuing importance to the US and the wider world. His remarks echoed a message issued by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Pakistan’s Independence Day, in which he specifically referred to the two countries’ cooperation on regional mediation, along with critical minerals, energy, counterterrorism, cultural heritage, and trade and investment. The reference to regional mediation is particularly significant given Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts involving Washington and Tehran. Islamabad has sought to use its relations with both sides to facilitate dialogue and help ease tensions between the United States and Iran. The ceremony also included an investiture ceremony for Waqar Ali Khan, who received the President’s Award for Pride of Performance in recognition of his decades of service as a community leader and cultural ambassador in the US. title: Mir Raza Ali's father seeks suspension of East DIG, others for 'concealing evidence'
description: Mir Hussain seeks suspenion of Ferozabad SHO. Says police officers “played a game” with him. Ali's family sought analysis of his smartwatch at PFSA.Mir Hussain Ali, the father of slain 25-year-old...
content: Published August 14, 2026 Mir Hussain Ali, the father of slain 25-year-old businessman Mir Raza Ali, on Friday demanded that Karachi East Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Dr Farrukh Ali and others be suspended for allegedly delaying the investigation and attempting to conceal evidence. Talking to journalists, Mir Hussain urged the authorities to also suspend the Ferozabad station house officer for his alleged role in mishandling the murder case of his son. He said that the police officers “played a game” with the bereaved family. Ali, an IBA graduate and businessman, was found dead in Gulistan-e-Jauhar a day after he went missing on July 28. Initially, police were working on the possibility that he had died by suicide; however, his father maintained that his son had been kidnapped, tortured and killed. A day earlier, the family of the deceased businessman opposed the forensic examination of his smartwatch by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) as their lawyer Jibran Nasir had sought analysis of the device at the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA). Speaking to Geo News, Nasir had said the smartwatch had remained in the possession of the former committee head for several days before being handed over to the NCCIA on Wednesday. The lawyer had said the family did not want the smartwatch examined by the NCCIA and instead wanted it forensically analysed at the PFSA, a Lahore-based facility operating under the Punjab Home Department. Nasir had also raised concerns about possible tampering, citing the fact that the smartwatch had remained with the former committee head for several days. The new investigation committee held its meeting at Ferozabad police station on Thursday, according to investigation sources. Several key decisions regarding the investigation were made during the meeting, and committee members were assigned specific responsibilities, the sources had added. Following the meeting, committee members proceeded to the incident site to collect additional evidence as part of the ongoing investigation. The sources had said the previous investigating officer also accompanied the team to assist with the inquiry. The committee chief, DIG Karachi Branch, was briefed on the investigation. This marked the DIG's first visit to the incident site since assuming leadership of the committee. Committee members also interviewed the nursery staff and gathered further details relevant to the case, according to investigation sources. Meanwhile, the new investigation team, headed by Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Amir Farooqi, had written four separate letters to the NCCIA, according to investigation sources. The team had requested a forensic examination of the deceased businessman's smartwatch, according to the contents of the letters. It had also sought details of Ali's social media accounts and other digital accounts, the sources said. The new investigation team would hold its second meeting at Ferozabad police station, sources had said. Following the meeting, the team would revisit the crime scene as part of its ongoing investigation. title: Unofficial results: PPP, PML-N bag one seat each from AJK's Bagh district
description: Voting took place at nine stations in LA-15, 14 in LA-16.Elections at the polling station had been postponed on Aug 10.PML-N and PPP have won 24 and 11 seats, respectively, so far.The Pakistan Peoples Party and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz ...
content: Published August 15, 2026 The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) have clinched one seat each in Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s (AJK) Bagh district, show unofficial results. According to unverified and unofficial results from all 186 polling stations in LA-16, PML-N candidate Mir Akbar Khan won the seat by securing 20,793 votes, followed by PPP’s Qamar Zaman Khan, who received 16,964 votes. In LA-15 Bagh-II, PPP’s Zia Qamar emerged victorious with 17,019 votes, while his closest contender, PML-N’s Mushtaq Minhas, secured 15,127 votes. Balloting began at 8am and continued uninterrupted until 5pm. People exercised their democratic right at nine polling stations in LA-15 Bagh-2 and 14 stations in LA-16 Bagh-3 today. The election had been postponed at the stations on August 10 after polling staff failed to arrive amid tensions. The AJK Election Commission had decided to hold Legislative Assembly elections for 45 seats, including 12 refugee seats, in three phases. In the first phase, elections were held across 13 constituencies in Mirpur Division. The second phase of the AJK elections took place on August 2, with polling held in eight constituencies of Muzaffarabad Division and all 12 refugee constituencies amid rigging allegations. The electoral process in LA-27 (Muzaffarabad-I) and LA-27 was postponed due to heavy rain and landslides. The PML-N emerged as the dominant party in AJK following the first two phases of the region's elections. With the latest results, PML-N’s tally has risen to 25 seats, while PPP has secured 11. Polling for the third phase of the AJK elections was held in four constituencies across Bagh and Haveli districts of Poonch division on August 10. According to the AJK Election Commission, Awami Dast-o-Baazo party's Sajid Iqbal Abbasi won the elections from LA-14 Bagh-I. PPP leader and AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore remained successful on LA-17 Bagh IV, defeating PML-N’s Mohsin Aziz. The AJK election commission withheld results of LA-16 Bagh-III and LA-15 Bagh-II as polling could not be held at some of the polling stations on August 10. Copyright © 2026. Geo Television Network. title: Australia v Bangladesh: Mehidy Hasan Miraz inspires visitors to historic first Test win in Australia - BBC Sport
description: Bangladesh thrash Australia by nine wickets on the fourth day of the series-opener in Darwin to complete one of Test cricket's greatest upsets.
content: Hasan Mahmud (right) was named player of the match after taking nine wickets in the opening Test First Test, Darwin (day four of five) Australia 198: (Smith 71; Mahmud 6-55) & 284 (Green 104; Miraz 5-66) Bangladesh 426: (Tanzid 101, Shanto 84, Miraz 65; Hazlewood 6-89) & 57-1 (Mominul 30*) Bangladesh win by nine wickets Scorecard Bangladesh thrashed Australia by nine wickets on the fourth day of the series-opener in Darwin to complete one of Test cricket's greatest upsets. After bowling the hosts out for 284 and needing 57 to win, Mominul Haque cut Beau Webster to the boundary for the winning runs to seal the nation's first Test victory in Australia. The moment sparked jubilation among Bangladesh players and staff as they celebrated arguably their greatest victory in 26 years of competing in Test cricket. Australia are the top-ranked Test nation while Bangladesh haven't played a series under the five-day format in the country since a 2-0 defeat in 2003. The visitors were on top of the match throughout, but it was spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz who took the spotlight on day four as he took 5-66 to dismiss Australia for 284, leaving just 57 runs needed to win. All-rounder Cameron Green showed fight with a valiant 104 but after being bowled by Hasan Mahmud, Australia's faint hopes of saving the Test all but disappeared. Seamer Mahmud was named player of the match after claiming 6-55 in the first innings and 3-56 in the second. "This is the biggest win so far for Bangladesh in any format," captain Najmul Hossain Shanto said. "Going forward we want to do something special in the future. I'm very happy, proud of myself and the way the boys played. We did a lot of hard work." Speaking on ABC, commentator Jim Maxwell described the result as one of the most "embarrassing defeats that Australia have ever suffered in Test cricket". History for Bangladesh as they beat Australia in Darwin Miraz's second innings performance followed a gritty 65 with the bat on day three that helped Bangladesh into a healthy first innings lead, before he dismissed talisman Steve Smith in Australia's second innings to set up victory. The spinner continued his form on day four as he had wicketkeeper Alex Carey caught behind for 30 before bowling all-rounder Webster for five with a pair of sumptuous deliveries to bring Australia's tail into play. The 28-year-old then had Australia captain Pat Cummins caught in close for eight, before a defiant 43-run eighth-wicket partnership between Green and Mitchell Starc was ended when Taskin Ahmed had the latter caught behind for 18. Green dug in for his third Test century in his home country in a timely knock amid criticism of his place in the side, but after being dismissed by Mahmud, Miraz removed Nathan Lyon to leave Bangladesh in touching distance of victory. Despite losing opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim for a duck to Josh Hazlewood in the second over, Mominul's unbeaten 30 and Shadman Islam's 25 sealed the resounding win. "They outplayed us in all facets, they were patient and disciplined," said Cummins. "I thought our prep was spot-on, no excuses." Australia's only previous Test defeat by Bangladesh was at Mirpur in 2017. The match was the first of a two-Test series, with the second beginning on 22 August (01:00 BST), which you can follow with live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra. Australia v Bangladesh 22-26 August Live ball-by-ball commentary on BBC Sounds, BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra from 00:30 BST each day (UK users only) The result was all the more remarkable as Bangladesh, who are the ninth-ranked Test team, had been bowled out for just 54 by a Cricket Australia XI in a warm-up match in Darwin days earlier. In June, they were thrashed by Zimbabwe, the lowest of cricket's 10-ranked Test-playing nations, in a one-off match in Harare. Bangladesh's prime minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the team on a video call with the players. "We're all eagerly waiting to welcome you home," he said on social media. Bangladesh also went into the match against a full-strength Australian team with two of their leading fast bowlers, Nahid Rana and Shoriful Islam, out injured. Shanto said the remarkable victory was helped by a mindset shift among his side's pacemen. "Five years ago, pacers didn't want to play Tests," said Shanto. "But we've been playing lots of Test cricket and they are giving importance to Test format. They want to play, want to perform, want to be world class. That is the mindset they now have. "Seniors like Mushfiqur [Rahim] and Mominul [Haque] have encouraged them to play more Test cricket." title: Pakistan says Islamabad MoU 'only way forward' amid US-Iran tensions
description: DPM Dar stresses dialogue, diplomacy for lasting regional peace.US envoy appreciates Pakistan's role in promoting stability.Dar, UK envoy discuss regional developments and cooperation.ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has renewed its call for...
content: Published August 15, 2026 ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has renewed its call for full implementation of the June 18 Islamabad memorandum of understanding, telling Washington that the agreement offered the "only way forward" towards regional peace and stability. The same message was also conveyed to the United Kingdom. Though Friday was a national holiday as the nation celebrated its 79 years of independence, the office of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar remained open and US Charge d'Affaires Natalie A Baker called on him on Friday, The News reported on Saturday. Pakistan's message to Washington comes at a time when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened Iran with economic isolation "like the world has never seen before", saying new measures are expected next week. It will be a combination of economic isolation like the world has never seen before. The foreign minister appreciated the positive trajectory in Pakistan-US relations and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy for lasting peace. "He stressed that the implementation of the Islamabad MoU of 18 June in letter and spirit is the only way forward," the Foreign Office said in a statement. Dar also reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to regional peace and security while safeguarding its national interests. "Discussions centred on Pakistan-US bilateral cooperation and recent regional developments. The US Chargé appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability and conveyed felicitations to the DPM/FM on Pakistan's Independence Day," added the statement. Meanwhile, the meeting between Baker and Dar was followed by UK High Commissioner to Pakistan Jane Marriott calling on the foreign minister. "Recent regional and international developments also figured in the discussion. DPM/FM stressed that the Islamabad MoU should be implemented by the parties in letter and spirit and reaffirmed that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only way forward to address outstanding issues," said the FO. Dar appreciated the positive momentum in Pakistan-UK relations while also recalling his recent meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on the sidelines of the ASEAN Regional Forum in Manila and highlighted the importance of sustained high-level contacts. They discussed key areas of mutual interest and ways to further strengthen bilateral cooperation. Ambassador of China Jiang Zaidong also called on the foreign minister, who conveyed condolences on the tragic death of a Chinese mountaineer following an avalanche incident at Broad Peak in Gilgit-Baltistan and promised full facilitation for the return of the deceased’s remains. Ambassador Jiang Zaidong appreciated Pakistan’s prompt assistance and support following the incident. "Views were also exchanged on regional developments and other matters of mutual interest while Ambassador Jiang Zaidong extended warm congratulations to the people and leadership of Pakistan on the occasion of Independence Day, reaffirming the close and time-tested ties between the two countries," said the statement. Earlier, the foreign minister spoke on the telephone with his Egyptian counterpart Badr Abdelatty, who extended warm greetings on Pakistan’s Independence Day to the leadership, government and people of Pakistan, and conveyed his best wishes for continued peace, progress and prosperity. "The two leaders reaffirmed the close and brotherly relations between Pakistan and Egypt and expressed their shared commitment to further strengthening cooperation across all areas of mutual interest, including through enhanced high-level exchanges and close institutional engagement. "They also exchanged views on regional and international developments of mutual interest and agreed to remain in close contact," said the Foreign Office. Copyright © 2026. Geo Television Network. title: Leavitt and Ocasio-Cortez spark conversation on challenges of family and career - BBC News
description: The White House press secretary quit this week to be with her children, while Democrat Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez said she was freezing her eggs.
content: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt and Congresswoman Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez have both spoken in recent days about balancing their careers with motherhood Last summer, Representative Sara Jacobs would run up to her office to give herself injections of hormones before rushing back to Congress for a session with her fellow lawmakers. The shots were for the second round of freezing her eggs, a medical procedure that can give women more time to have children. "It was an empowering decision that gave me more agency," the 37-year-old said, adding that the process was challenging. "Your body hurts. Your hormones are crazy. It's kind of like puberty and menopause at the same time." Jacobs announced she was beginning the egg freezing process in 2021, at a time when she said few lawmakers were discussing the topic in the halls of Congress. The process - which can cost more than $10,000 (£7,400) and is rarely covered by insurance - involves doctors harvesting eggs from the ovaries and freezing them for a future pregnancy. This week, Democratic Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez announced she too was beginning the process of freezing her eggs , documenting the daily mechanics of giving herself hormone shots on social media. Watch: Key moments from Karoline Leavitt's White House tenure The left-wing Democrat's announcement sparked a conversation about the challenges of balancing motherhood and a demanding career, the same week that White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced she would be leaving the Trump administration to spend more time with her family, including her infant. "The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy and attention required of [being] the White House press secretary," Leavitt said. Leavitt brought her son Nicholas, or "Niko", into the White House press briefing room during Thanksgiving last year Several women with busy careers spoke to the BBC about the challenges of juggling their work with motherhood in the only industrialised nation that does not mandate paid parental leave. Less than a quarter of workers in the US have access to paid family leave through their employer, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. More than 120 nations around the world - including all European countries - provide paid maternity leave. In the US, women are increasingly having children at older ages, while more are choosing not to have children at all. From 2016 to 2023, the average age of all mothers giving birth in the US rose from 28.7 to 29.6, according to a 2025 report from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Michele Heisler (left) says raising her children while working as a professor of medicine meant long nights, and lots of help Michele Heisler, a professor of internal medicine at the University of Michigan, gave birth to her first child after going back to medical school at the age of 30. She was pregnant with her son during her third year of medical school. Heisler, who serves as medical director for non-profit Physicians for Human Rights, said she had only been able to dedicate enough time to her career because of access to resources - including nannies - and a husband who was an equal partner in parenting. "Unless it's clear that both are equal parents, [child rearing] is always going to fall on the woman, and then you're going to have to take a step back in some way," Heisler said. Heisler said a flexible schedule is what allowed her to pursue her career to the fullest - staying up late at night to work and waking up sometimes at 05:00 to get her research done - so she could spend time with her children. Legal scholar Seema Patel says she stays up late to finish work after her children are in bed Seema Patel, an associate professor of law at UC Law San Francisco, also stays up late at night to try to finish her work so she doesn't have to miss moments with her children. "The reality is that these years in your kids' lives are so fleeting, and I'm super aware of the time," she said. Patel worked for San Francisco's Office of Labor Standards Enforcement, which became the first local government in the US to pass a law requiring employers to provide paid parental leave. But through her career as a workers' rights lawyer, she has seen many lower-wage workers and parents who are not lucky enough to have access to paid time off. When Patel began working as a federal attorney, her boss advised her to save up her vacation days in case she eventually wanted to have children and needed to take leave. She ended up taking the advice. "I was a brand new, young attorney who had not even contemplated that stage of my life, but I had to in that moment, face that question of - I better be saving my vacation days," she said. But even with some maternity leave and a dedicated partner, as her children - now ages 13, 11 and seven - have grown older, the work-life juggling act remains a challenge. "I have a high-producing job," she said. "How can I do that while also being there for my kids and attentive to them? I don't have an answer." Congresswoman Sara Jacobs documented her journey freezing her eggs on social media For now, Jacobs, who has completed two rounds of egg freezing, plans to hold off on having children while her job requires her to fly across the country from California to Washington. "Figuring out how to be a mum when I'm gone half the time across the country, it's logistically complicated," she said. Jacobs said she was impressed by her fellow lawmakers who have managed to make it work. Only a handful of women have given birth while in Congress, while a few dozen lawmakers are mothers to children under the age of 18. The federal government, like many US employers, does not offer paid parental leave, Jacobs noted. "Both Congress and the general American workplace were designed by and for men who had often stay-at-home spouses who handled all of the domestic work," she said. "It's going to take a lot of work for us to create a society where the domestic work is really shared equally between women and men." In the meantime, Jacobs feels reassured to have a back-up plan for whenever she does feel she can fit children into her busy career. "I hope to be able to do that one day, but I just haven't figured the time is right just yet." Who could replace White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt? title: Medal ceremonies delayed at European Athletics Championships in Birmingham due to arrest - BBC News
description: Transport was also delayed because of the arrest, leading to crowds building up outside the venue.
content: Thousands of members of the crowd were unable to leave the event as transport was suspended Medal ceremonies at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham were postponed after a man was arrested on suspicion of fraud. West Midlands Police said concerns were raised after a man was found in an area of Alexander Stadium on Saturday evening without the right accreditation. Transport at the tournament was suspended as a result of the arrest and necessary security procedures. Members of the crowd reported being held outside by security staff for more than an hour after the event finished, with a large police presence at the scene. The evening session concluded with Great Britain winning a pair of gold medals in the men's and women's 4x100m relays. Tournament organisers said transport was suspended while the necessary security measures took place, but operations had returned to normal in the early hours of Sunday. A statement from Birmingham 2026 said: "The safety and wellbeing of our spectators, athletes, workforce and the wider Championships' family will always be our first priority. "We recognise that the delays presented challenges for those affected and would like to thank everyone for their patience, understanding and cooperation throughout the evening." More information relating to the postponed medal ceremonies is due to be released later. A West Midlands Police spokesperson said a man in his 30s remained in custody for questioning. The crowd at the Alexander Stadium appeared to be near its 23,000 capacity. At one point during the session, there was an announcement that the six medal ceremonies, scheduled to take place after the final event between 22:00 and 23:00 BST were cancelled, understood to be in relation to the police incident. People posted on social media, reporting "crazy queues" for the shuttle bus and blue flashing lights on the main road outside the stadium. A statement on the event's official account, posted on X at 23:03, said: "We apologise for the significant delays in leaving the Alexander Stadium venue this evening. "Buses and coaches will start to arrive and departures will begin to gradually take place. "We thank you for your patience with this matter. Please listen to the instructions from the safety personnel and marshals who are there to support you." title: UK assures Pakistan of swift action on students’ visa delays - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
description: Stresses the need to remove obstacles faced by Pakistani students seeking education abroad and facilitate them.
content: Get the latest news and updates from Dawn ISLAMABAD: The federal law and justice minister raised the issue of delays in UK visas for Pakistani students while the British high commissioner assured resolution of the issue. British High Commissioner Jane Marriott called on Federal Minister for Law & Justice Senator Azam Nazeer Tarar. The meeting discussed Pakistan-UK bilateral relations, matters of mutual interest and ways to further strengthen cooperation between the two countries, says a press release issued here. It said that during the meeting, the minister raised the issue of delays in UK visas for Pakistani students and conveyed the government’s concern to the British High Commissioner. The law minister said that hundreds of Pakistani students were facing difficulties due to delays in visa processing, with a risk that the delays could result in the loss of their academic year. He stressed the need to remove obstacles faced by Pakistani students seeking education abroad and facilitate them in this regard. The minister briefed the British high commissioner that, on the directives of the prime minister, a committee under his chairmanship was working to improve the legal and institutional framework concerning Pakistani students studying abroad. He further informed the high commissioner that, on the prime minister’s directives, the committee had finalised its recommendations on the matter, and work was underway to further improve the legal and institutional framework for Pakistani students pursuing education abroad. The minister said that the legal and institutional framework for Pakistani students seeking education abroad was being improved to develop an effective mechanism for addressing the issues faced by students. Ms Marriott assured the Federal Minister that the issue of delays in visas for Pakistani students would be addressed. The meeting also discussed further strengthening educational linkages between Pakistan and the United Kingdom, as well as enhancing institutional cooperation and engagement between the two countries. The press release said that Minister of State for Law, Justice and Human Rights Barrister Aqeel Malik was also present during the meeting. title: Avalanche risk, bad weather disrupt climbing season in Gilgit-Baltistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
description: No climber managed to summit K2, Gasherbrum-I this summer.
content: Get the latest news and updates from Dawn GILGIT: Climate change-induced shifts in weather patterns have worsened conditions on the peaks of the Karakoram Range in Gilgit-Baltistan, creating serious difficulties for mountaineers. No climber managed to summit the world’s second-highest mountain, K2 (8,611 metres), or Gasherbrum-I (8,080 metres), this summer. Around 40 foreign climbers also failed to reach the summits of Gasherbrum-II (8,035 metres), Broad Peak (8,047 metres) and Nanga Parbat (8,126 metres) this year. Persistent storms, heavy snowfall, unstable snow conditions and an exceptionally high avalanche risk created hurdles for climbers attempting to summit peaks in Gilgit-Baltistan, particularly five of the 14 eight-thousanders. No climber managed to summit K2, Gasherbrum-I this summer Expedition teams usually spend weeks at base camps assessing weather forecasts, fixing ropes and acclimatising before beginning their summit push. Mountaineers have experienced persistent bad weather, avalanches, rockfalls, strong winds and unpredictable conditions at the peaks during the summer season for the past two years. The climbing season on the Karakoram peaks, including K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum-I and Gasherbrum-II, usually runs from the end of July to mid-August. ‘Over 200 attempted’ Ghulam Muhammad, a tour operator, told Dawn that more than 200 climbers attempted to summit K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum-II and Gasherbrum-I this year. “This year, continued bad weather kept teams at base camp, while repeated summit attempts were called off due to unsafe conditions on the mountains.” He said only three foreign expedition groups reached the summit of Gasherbrum-II, while members of one local expedition team successfully summited Broad Peak. Earlier, two expedition teams had summited Nanga Parbat, where the climbing season closes by the end of June. Ayaz Shigri, general secretary of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, told Dawn that weather conditions at the peaks remained unstable this summer. However, he said that after the devastating tragedy at Broad Peak on July 30, in which 10 foreign climbers, including Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, lost their lives when a snow avalanche struck them during their summit attempt, many climbers at K2 and Gasherbrum-I abandoned their missions and joined the search and rescue operation. Asghar Porik, another tour operator, said shifting weather patterns in the mountains had made it difficult for mountaineers to plan their summit attempts. “For 100 or 500 years, climbers have planned their attempts in the Karakoram according to established weather patterns. They usually attempt K2 between July 20 and August 15, with the weather generally considered suitable until the end of June,” he said. He said the situation had worsened in recent years as rising temperatures made snow unstable and increased the risks of avalanches and rockfalls. Asghar Porik added that his 11-member expedition team at Gasherbrum-II could not find a suitable weather window and called off its expedition. Ikram Baig, president of the GB Association of Tour Operators, said Broad Peak was considered one of the comparatively less dangerous eight-thousanders. “Broad Peak is often described by experienced mountaineers as one of the comparatively less technical 8,000-metre peaks. However, fresh snowfall can make even an easier route extremely dangerous by creating unstable snow conditions and a high risk of avalanches,” he said. Mr Baig said climate change had altered conditions and made the environment at the peaks increasingly uncertain. Mohammad Ali Nagari, a tour operator, said the growing number of commercial expeditions was also degrading the fragile environment at the peaks. Ayaz Shigri said the summer climbing season on the Karakoram peaks had now closed, with climbers returning from the eight-thousanders without summiting K2 or Gasherbrum-I this year. Last year, too, foreign climbers faced similar conditions and mostly returned without summiting peaks in GB. title: Formula E: Taylor Barnard on the end-of-season races in London - BBC News
description: Taylor Barnard, 22, says talented young drivers often get shut out because of financial issues.
content: Taylor Barnard is the youngest driver to secure a podium, pole and points in Formula E Making split-second decisions while driving up to 200mph probably seems like a crazy task for most of us. But Britain's youngest Formula E driver is learning to take it in his stride as his second season in the series draws to a close. Back in 2024, Taylor Barnard became the youngest person to start an E-Prix and since then he's broken several other records - including becoming the youngest driver to secure a podium, pole and points in the sport. So what's the 22-year-old got his sights set on now? The ultimate title, of course, world champion. Barnard tells BBC Newsbeat he feels he got into racing by the "skin of my teeth", due to the extreme costs it takes to climb the motorsport ladder. The immense financial backing needed to become a professional driver has been long known, with stars like Sir Lewis Hamilton speaking openly about the sacrifices his family made to get him a seat in Formula 1. And Barnard feels if he was trying to climb the ranks now, he wouldn't make it due to prices being "so blown out of proportion". Barnard says fans can expect to see a lot of the cars going "side-by-side [at] almost every corner" Barnard, who's from Norwich, says the driving bug was passed down from his father, who was a karting driver in his younger years. He rose through the ranks of British and European karting, before his talent helped him secure backing to get through Formula 3 and 2. Barnard finally secured a seat in Formula E with McLaren, and transferred to DS Penske for the current season. "It sounds very simple but trust me, it's anything but that," he says. "It's super expensive, super difficult. And where my family and I've come from, we've always been on the difficult end of that journey." The driver recalls being raised in a "very normal, working family", and at one stage they had to re-mortgage their house so Barnard could continue his racing career. "We really did put everything on the line for me to be able to make it," he says. "I would be lying if we're still not stinging from when we did that." Now that he's getting paid as a professional, he says he's trying to pay his parents back "for everything they've done". Barnard also wants to support young talented drivers who he feels are being left behind - as he feels not everybody that's made it into top-flight sports "deserves to be there". "There's definitely people that have bought their way in or haven't earned their way," he says. "And there's definitely been people out there, younger guys or girls that have the talent and the skill to be able to make it, which just gets shut out by financial issues. "That's not right. And the way that it's going in the last few years, it's only getting worse." Barnard says he's not sure how motorsport's governing body the FIA or racing teams can best address this issue as he recognises it is a business. There are various academies and driver development programmes run by professional teams, but they are often very competitive. An FIA spokesperson told Newsbeat "improving accessibility and affordability in motorsport is a core priority" for the governing body. They added that some costs connected with competing, such as travel and team operations, were "outside the FIA's direct remit" but it was "committed to taking decisive action and investing in global initiatives". Among the programmes, it said, its affordable cross car, girls on track and global karting plan look to lower "financial barriers" and expand "access to talented drivers around the world". Barnard made his Formula E debut with McLaren, but raced for DS Penske this season Barnard's journey has made him "appreciate the little things a lot more", he says. And the end of this season will be made sweeter as he gets to drive in front of his family and friends at his home race when the 2025-2026 series closes at London's Excel this weekend. It will be a tense double-header as nine drivers were in contention for the championship title going into the last two races. Barnard's future for next season is still slightly uncertain as DS Automobiles, the manufacturer behind his team, is set to leave the sport. And with Penske yet to confirm its plans for the next era of Formula E cars, dubbed Gen4, the young Brit is focused on finishing the season on a high. Barnard says fans can expect to see a lot of the grid going "side-by-side [at] almost every corner" and probably "a few crashes". "Throughout the weekend we obviously do the duals in qualifying, which is super exciting. "Next year the cars are going to be even faster, which is going to be even more exciting. "I would actually argue Formula E has the best racing that you can view anywhere." Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here . title: Twelve killed as Polish bus veers off Hungarian motorway - BBC News
description: Dozens more are seriously injured after the tourist bus overturned in the early hours of Sunday morning.
content: Footage shows wreckage of Polish tourist bus Twelve people were killed and dozens more injured when a bus carrying Polish pilgrims veered off a Hungarian motorway and into a ditch. Police said the bus overturned after coming off the M3 motorway, which connects Hungary's capital Budapest with the north-eastern city of Nyíregyháza, at around 01:00 local time on Sunday (23:00 GMT on Saturday). Officers believe the driver fell asleep at the wheel. He has been taken into custody. Thirty-five out of the 57 passengers and two drivers onboard have been rescued by firefighters so far, state media reports. Emergency services had been attempting to lift the rear axle of the 24-tonne bus to remove the people trapped underneath before cranes arrived to lift the whole vehicle, according to Hungarian news agency MTI. Hungary's ambulance service said it had treated one person with life-threatening injuries, nine people with serious injuries and a further 37 people with minor injuries. The country's Prime Minister Péter Magyar offered his "sincere condolences" to the families of the victims and wished those injured a speedy recovery. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk echoed his sentiments, adding he had decided to send a "special" Polish aircraft with foreign ministry officials and medical services. "We are together in this difficult moment," he added. The bus had been returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina, and had been carrying pilgrims from Poland's southernmost region of Podkarpacie, according to Polish news agency PAP. Poland's Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said his Hungarian counterpart had told him police had already begun questioning the bus driver. title: FPCCI demands rollback of high taxes on hybrid cars - Business - DAWN.COM
description: Calls for notifying new auto policy immediately.
content: Get the latest news and updates from Dawn HYDERABAD: The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) has expressed concern over the sales tax hike on hybrid vehicles, from 8.5 per cent to 25pc, and warned that this short-sighted policy would hurt consumers and cripple the auto industry. In a statement issued on Saturday, Adeel Siddiqui, a member of the FPCCI Executive Committee, noted that tax concessions on hybrid vehicles expired on June 30 and with no new auto policy notified in time, the Federal Board of Revenue restored the general sales tax rate of 25pc on hybrid electric vehicles and plug-in hybrid vehicles. He said that this represented a massive increase from earlier preferential rates of 8.5pc for hybrids up to 1800cc and 12.75pc for those above 1800cc. So, he said, the auto industry was in chaos and automakers have temporarily halted production and stopped issuing invoices because they do not know which sales tax rate to apply. Calls for notifying new auto policy immediately He said that a production halt affected thousands of workers, vendors, and transporters, as well as factory workers, who were losing work and wages due to this policy vacuum. He stated that Pakistan’s energy security was at risk, as it imports about 80pc of its petroleum products, making transport electrification a matter of national security. He said that the government was discouraging fuel-efficient vehicles and keeping the country dependent on expensive imported fuel by making hybrids more expensive. Secondly, he said, investor confidence was eroding, and policy uncertainty was damaging it in new-energy vehicle projects. He said that policy remained regressive, wondering why the government was increasing taxes on hybrids — which offer lower running costs and reduced fuel consumption — while reportedly considering tax relief on vehicles priced above Rs10m. He said that this sends a confusing signal about the government’s policy priorities. He called for an immediate rollback of 25pc sales tax on hybrid vehicles, or at least a reduction to 18pc until the new auto policy was finalised. He demanded that Auto Policy 2026-31 should be notified without delay to provide clarity and stability to the industry. He stressed the need for a phased transition to clean energy with incentives tied to local manufacturing and technology transfer. He said that current policy was a self-inflicted wound that would slow Pakistan’s transition to fuel-efficient vehicles, increase fuel import costs, and damage the auto industry at a time when it was showing signs of recovery. He said that it was high time to act before damage was done to Pakistan’s automotive sector and energy security. title: South Korean president proposes talks with North to formally end war - World - DAWN.COM
description: Two countries are still at war since their 1950s confrontation ended without a peace treaty.
content: Get the latest news and updates from Dawn SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed talks with North Korea on Saturday to formally end the long-running Korean war, as Pyongyang deepens ties with Moscow while asserting its status as an “irreversible” nuclear state. The two Koreas remain technically at war because their 1950-53 conflict ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty. Lee made the proposal in his speech at a ceremony marking the anniversary of Korea’s liberation from Japan’s 1910-45 colonial rule. “Let us put down our intention to threaten each other and begin discussions to end the long-running war as the directly involved parties,” Lee said in his speech. Two countries are still at war since their 1950s confrontation ended without a peace treaty “Through this, it may also be possible to discuss effective measures to halt the advancement of North Korea’s nuclear capabilities,” he added. Lee’s proposal came as North Korea this week denounced upcoming annual US-South Korean military drills, warning of stronger deterrence measures. Pyongyang has also recently been bristling over Tokyo’s gradual military build-up in the Pacific, firing off two missiles in as many weeks after the latter pledged to up its defence capabilities with a “sense of urgency and crisis”. North Korea has repeatedly declared itself an “irreversible” nuclear state since a 2019 summit between Kim and US counterpart Donald Trump in Hanoi collapsed over the scope of denuclearisation and sanctions relief. South Korea’s dovish President Lee has reversed the stance of his hawkish predecessor since taking power in June last year, offering the nuclear-armed North talks without preconditions. Last month, South Korea’s unification minister even claimed Seoul had abandoned its campaign prioritising pressure on the North to dismantle its nuclear weapons, focusing instead on halting the expansion of Pyongyang’s nuclear activities. The hermetic leadership of North Korea has yet to respond to Lee’s repeated offers, and has instead bolstered military ties with Russia. Analysts say Pyongyang is receiving financial support, food, energy and military technology from Moscow for supplying troops and munitions for Russia’s war in Ukraine. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is expected to visit Russia later this year, potentially to discuss further weapons supplies to Moscow. Washington, Seoul’s key security ally, stations about 28,500 troops in South Korea to bolster the country’s defences against military threats from Pyongyang. Colonel Ryan Donald, spokesman for the US and South Korean combined forces command, said this week that North Korea’s deployment to the European war had changed the threat his soldiers may face on the Korean peninsula. “They’ve taken those lessons they learned there and brought them back to North Korea,” he told reporters as he talked about the 11-day South Korea-US joint exercises due to begin on Monday. “Our training accounts for that threat.” Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026 Compunode.com Pvt. title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: POLITICS OF THE BIG TENT - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
description: The very diversity that makes big-tent parties electorally powerful can also become their greatest vulnerability.
content: Get the latest news and updates from Dawn In Europe and the United States, the post-1945 era marked a shift from ‘mass parties’ to broad ‘big-tent’ parties. Mass parties had operated on strict class lines. Democratic socialist outfits appealed to industrial workers, while conservative parties represented business elites and religious traditionalists. Big-tent politics had already taken root in North America due to its vast geography, rapid industrialisation, and diverse immigrant and Black populations. To build winning national majorities, the Democratic and Republican parties developed broad platforms, accommodating competing internal factions under a shared umbrella and a loose ideological core. This was the beginning of big-tent parties. The Democratic Party in the US, especially from the early 1930s onwards, has housed democratic socialists, progressives, social liberals and pro-business centrists, alongside its conservative Southern wing, which existed within the party till the early 1960s. The latter was mainly to bag votes from the ‘Bible belt’ states. The modern Republican Party functions as a broad umbrella encompassing social conservatives, Christian nationalists, fiscal centrists and right-wing populists. A similar evolution occurred in western Europe after World War II. According to the German jurist Otto Kirchheimer, as the post-war economic growth expanded the middle-class, most voters began to favour pragmatic moderation over class antagonism. Left-wing parties, such as the UK Labour Party and Germany’s Social Democratic Party, shifted toward a progressive centre-left stance, while centre-right parties, such as the British Conservatives and Germany’s Christian Democrats, softened their hard social moralism and elitism to capture votes from across the classes. Political scientists mostly view big-tent parties as important democratic stabilisers. By absorbing diverse economic, regional and social groups, a big-tent outfit facilitates them to negotiate and form a consensus under a single umbrella. This prevents extreme polarisation and avoids the chaotic parliamentary fragmentation typical of unstable multiparty systems that lack big-tent parties. From the Democrats and Republicans in the United States to the PPP, PML-N and PTI in Pakistan, the very diversity that makes big-tent parties electorally powerful can also become their greatest vulnerability Big-tent outfits combine diverse demands and elements, transforming societal rivalries into organised, workable governing units. The success of a big-tent party depends on how they design mechanisms to manage internal dissent. Rather than enforcing monolithic obedience, party structures use primary elections, regional quotas and factional appointments to give diverse interest groups a seat at tables that matter. This internal diplomacy allows the overarching party to remain flexible. A well-managed big-tent party can position its platform across different political cycles, moving slightly leftward or rightward to keep pace with changing electorate moods, without suffering an electoral decline. Following the 1947 Partition , India saw a classic big-tent system emerge under the Indian National Congress (INC). Operating on a secular, centre-left platform, Congress absorbed diverse socialist, moderate and regional groups to maintain a 30-year political monopoly. As the nation’s founding party, it offered a shared national brand that co-opted multiple local political elites and bridged vast linguistic and religious divides. INC’s dominance was broken in 1977 by the Janata Party (JP). JP was a broad anti-INC coalition of secular, regional, Hindutva and left-wing groups who couldn’t find a place under INC’s tent. However, JP illustrated a common pitfall related to big-tent politics: unmanaged factional infighting. Driven by intense ideological friction and personal rivalries among its leadership, JP collapsed from within after just three years in power. When internal fractures widen in big-tent parties, the parties tend to lose their electoral appeal or fall prey to radical internal takeovers. This occurred within the US Republican Party, where the right-wing populist Maga (Make America Great Again) movement led by Donald Trump weaponised primary elections to displace the Republican Party’s dominant free market and moderate factions. The populist wing of the party then reoriented the outfit into becoming a nationalist-populist vehicle. But this transformation has introduced severe vulnerabilities, driven by infighting within the party’s populist wing, foreign policy controversies and an increasing backlash in the US against Israeli lobby groups such as the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac). Trump’s approval ratings have plummeted . The Democrats are facing their own internal tensions. Key primary victories by progressive candidates of the party have alarmed its centrist factions, who fear left-leaning Democrats could alienate moderate voters in upcoming national contests. In South Asia, apart from INC and then JP, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) began to function as a big-tent party. Historically a Hindu nationalist party with an upper-caste base, the BJP began to widen its umbrella. It started to accommodate distinct groups: Hindutva hardliners, big business groups, populists and pragmatists absorbed from opposition parties. Hindutva remains the BJP’s ideological anchor, though, even as it increasingly applies big-tent electoral strategies. Pakistan developed a big-tent model led by the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N). Before these, Pakistan’s founding party, the Muslim League, had successfully managed to combine a wide range of left to right groups to win enough seats in the 1946 elections in British India, which allowed it to push for a separate Muslim-majority country. But after the creation of Pakistan, friction between different groups in the League became so intense that the party fractured. The PPP, formed in 1967, shaped a centre-left core with diverse leftist, progressive, liberal and centrist groups, while the PML-N, formed in 1992, united urban pro-business cohorts, landed elites, centrists and social conservatives. In 2011, facilitated by the then military establishment, the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) expanded into a third big-tent party by absorbing traditional ‘electables’ from the two existing big-tent outfits. PTI operated as an archetypal contemporary populist party, weaving a flexible and performative core of right- and left-wing tropes around a central anti-corruption narrative and personal loyalty to its leader. This vague ideological architecture allowed urban middle-class youth, conservatives, landed elites and mainstream Islamists to coexist under one banner. However, like India’s Janata Party, PTI struggled to manage its internal frictions and rapidly unravelled once its top leader was removed from power and imprisoned. Big-tent parties remain double-edged constructs. While their capacity to combine diverse interests and build broad platforms shields democracies against fragmentation, their reliance on a conflicted ideological core and mismanaged internal conflicts leaves them vulnerable. This requires continuous maintenance. Without disciplined leadership, big-tent parties risk devolving into factional warfare, opening the door to radical takeovers or collapse when internal consensus breaks down. Maintaining a workable equilibrium remains a constant challenge. In Pakistan, big-tent parties such as the PML-N and the PPP have done remarkably well to avoid disintegration despite attempts by previous military establishments to dismantle them by exploiting their internal frictions. This ability to regroup and survive is something that PTI has, so far, failed to demonstrate. Published in Dawn, EOS, August 16th, 2026 Nadeem F. title: Mir Raza Ali murder case: Court directs investigators to complete probe until Aug 24
description: Additional evidence recovered from crime scene: investigation team.Court directs Ali's business partner to cooperate with investigators.Probe team retrieves digital devices from NCCIA, to be sent to PFSA.KARACHI: A judicial magistrate...
content: Published August 15, 2026 KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Saturday granted investigators until August 24 to complete the probe into the death of young businessman Mir Raza Ali after the investigating officer (IO) apprised the court that the inquiry had yet to be finalised. Ali, an IBA graduate and businessman, was found dead in Gulistan-e-Jauhar a day after he went missing on July 28. His father has maintained that his son was murdered and rejected suggestions that his death was a case of suicide. IO Siraj Lashari appeared before the East judicial magistrate and sought additional time to conclude the investigation and submit a report. The court accepted the request and directed investigators to present their findings at the next hearing on August 24. Investigation officials said that the committee also retrieved Ali's mobile phone and smartwatch from the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). The devices will now be sent to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) in Lahore for forensic examination. According to officials, the move comes after Ali's family expressed reservations about having the devices examined by the NCCIA and sought an independent forensic analysis. The officials added that additional evidence had been recovered from the crime scene; however, no further details were disclosed. Investigators probing the death of the young businessman have expanded the inquiry committee, increasing the members from 7 to 9. The newly inducted members include the SHO of Shah Latif Town police station and a deputy superintendent of police (DSP). In a separate development, an additional district and sessions judge extended the pre-arrest bail of Ali's business partner, Muhammad Ahmed, until August 24. During the hearing, Ahmed's counsel told the court that his client had been called to the crime scene at around 1am. The lawyer argued that his client feared being implicated in the case despite assisting the inquiry. The court later restrained police from harassing him pending further proceedings. After hearing arguments, the court extended the interim bail and directed Ahmed to cooperate with investigators and join the ongoing probe. Speaking to reporters outside the court, Jibran Nasir, counsel for the deceased businessman's father, said the victim's family had provided investigators with the names of individuals who might possess information relevant to the case but had not accused anyone of involvement in the killing. "The parents have not used the word 'suspect' for any individual," Nasir said, adding that names, including that of Ahmed, had been shared only to help investigators pursue all possible leads. He described the case as a "blind murder" and said the family did not want to level allegations without evidence. Nasir expressed confidence in the newly-constituted investigation team, saying its inquiry was not contradicting the available medical evidence and was being conducted in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs). He said the family wanted investigators to ensure accurate geo-fencing analysis, obtain relevant CCTV footage and complete forensic examinations. The lawyer also criticised the handling of the case by the previous investigation team, alleging that serious procedural lapses had occurred during the initial stages of the inquiry. He claimed that a crime scene unit had failed to reach the site and alleged that the scene had been set on fire, potentially affecting the collection of DNA evidence. "Our focus is on identifying the killers," he said, adding that the family wanted those responsible to be arrested alive and brought before the courts so the case could proceed through the legal process. title: Balochistan home minister's security convoy comes under fire in Mastung
description: Convoy was travelling from Kalat towards Quetta.Six injured security personnel shifted to hospital.Security personnel exchanged fire with attackers.QUETTA: Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langau's security convoy came...
content: Published August 14, 2026 QUETTA: Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langau’s security convoy came under fire while travelling from Kalat to Quetta, officials said on Friday. Mastung additional deputy commissioner said the convoy was targeted while travelling towards Quetta, while police said Langau remained safe in the firing. At least six personnel from the security squad were injured in the exchange of fire, according to police. The injured personnel were shifted to Nawab Ghous Bakhsh Hospital in Quetta for treatment, police said. Speaking after the attack, the Balochistan home minister vowed that the attack will not weaken their resolve. "I cannot be frightened by these firecrackers," Langau said while speaking in Quetta. The incident came around three weeks after a sessions judge and his gunman were killed when unidentified assailants opened fire on their vehicle in Mastung. An additional sessions judge and another person were also critically injured in the attack, an official said on July 23. According to District Police Officer (DPO) Allah Bakhsh Baloch, the judges were travelling from Quetta to the sessions court in Mastung when their vehicle came under fire in the Wali Khan area. Pakistan witnessed a surge in terror activities, particularly in its Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, since 2021, when the Afghan Taliban came into power. According to a report by the Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS), the two provinces remained the country's main hotspots for violence during the second quarter of 2026, with KP emerging as the worst-affected region. The report stated that KP and Balochistan together accounted for nearly 96% of all violence-related fatalities recorded during the quarter. Of the total deaths, more than 61% (475) were reported in KP, while Balochistan accounted for 34% (265). KP also recorded the highest number of violent incidents, with 151 cases, representing 57% of the nationwide total. Balochistan followed with 94 incidents, or 35%, underscoring the concentration of militant activity in the two provinces. Copyright © 2026. Geo Television Network. title: Police questioning Mir Raza Ali's 35 phone contacts: IO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
description: DSP Lashari tells court no one named as suspect yet; murder probe still underway.
content: Get the latest news and updates from Dawn KARACHI: Investigators probing the Mir Raza Ali murder case are questioning as many as 35 persons who were found to have been in contact with the deceased over the phone. The information was provided by the newly appointed investigating officer (IO), DSP Siraj Lashari, to a judicial magistrate on Saturday. Young businessman and IBA graduate Mir Raza had gone missing on July 28 and his bullet-riddled body was found a day later in bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. On Saturday, DSP Lashari appeared in court and sought more time to file a progress report as he took over the case just two days ago. DSP Lashari tells court no one named as accused yet; murder probe still underway He stated that around 35 suspects were being interrogated as the call data record reflected that they were in contact with the victim. He submitted that the police have yet to name anyone as accused since the investigation was still underway and more time was needed to conclude it. He sought more time to complete the investigation as well as to collect forensic and medical reports. The court granted him time to conclude the investigation and asked him to file a progress report on Aug 24. Business partner’s bail extended Also on Saturday, a sessions court extended the interim pre-arrest bail of Mir Raza’s business partner Muhammad Ahmed Bhardey till Aug 24. An additional district and sessions judge (East) had granted pre-arrest bail to the applicant against a surety of Rs100,000 till Aug 15. On Saturday, applicant’s counsel Khalid Mumtaz submitted that his client was being harassed by police and he might be arrested despite extending full cooperation with investigators. He informed the court that the applicant had been summoned to the crime scene rather than to a police station. Representing the deceased’s family, Advocate Jibran Nasir submitted that the police had merely summoned the applicant, along with around 35 others, for the investigation process. The judge questioned why the applicant had sought bail when he had not initially been named as an accused in the case. The court also made it clear that the applicant would have to join the investigation regardless of whether he remained on bail. The applicant informed the court that he had been appearing at the police station whenever the police called him. The judge directed him not to leave the city while the investigation was underway and extended his interim bail until Aug 24. Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026 Compunode.com Pvt. Ltd.
